CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Continue the constructive negotiating path opened at the G20 truce — hold our tariff posture unchanged, signal willingness to increase purchases of US agricultural/energy goods, and push for a settlement before the March 1 deadline rather than escalating. Avoid new retaliatory measures that would deepen damage to our already-strained export sector, and keep the Huawei/Meng file separate from the trade track to avoid torpedoing talks.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to China is high — tariffs now cover ~$250B of our exports at 10-25%, the Huawei/Meng arrest signals firm-level tech-supply targeting, and the real economy is already decelerating: November industrial production fell to 5.4% (its lowest since 2009), Q3 GDP was 6.5% (slowest since 2009), export growth halved, the RMB depreciated ~6% and equities lost ~20% (World Bank/Dec 2018 trade data). That justifies a +0.5 high-banded threat score. But it is not existential: we retain stimulus headroom (PBoC liquidity, fiscal/infrastructure), large reserves, and an active truce with talks that resumed Jan 7-8. Critically, the US is also under visible strain (consumer sentiment tumbled to 91.2, the 10Y yield fell from ~3.1 to 2.56, oil crashed to ~$46-52, credit spreads widened), so the terrain favors reaching a deal rather than escalation. Because our export economy is more exposed than the US to further tariff escalation, the rational stance is de-escalatory engagement that buys time and extracts a fair settlement, not retaliation: action_score +0.1, negotiate.
